Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings: 65-year-old woman with T2DM and hypertension presents with 5-day acute dry cough, green rhinorrhoea, subjective fever/chills, myalgias; no dyspnoea, chest pain, sputum, haemoptysis, or sore throat.  

Working diagnosis: Acute viral upper respiratory tract infection / viral bronchitis most likely. Differential includes COVID-19 infection and post-viral acute bacterial sinusitis. ACE-inhibitor–induced cough considered less likely given accompanying systemic and nasal symptoms.  

Plan:  
• Symptomatic management encouraged (continue Lemsip but avoid additional paracetamol products).  
• Advise purchase of thermometer and monitor temperature; red-flag safety-netting provided (temp > 37.5–38 °C persisting, worsening cough, purulent sputum, haemoptysis, shortness of breath, chest pain).  
• Educated that diabetes increases risk of secondary bacterial infection; instructed to seek review if deterioration occurs—possible need for antibiotics.  
• Reinforce regular diabetes and blood-pressure reviews with GP.  
• No immediate antibiotics or investigations indicated today.

Management Plan

- Education: Nature of viral URTI, expected course (1–2 weeks cough may persist), temperature monitoring, medication safety (paracetamol limits), when to re-present.  
- Medications: Continue current diabetes and hypertension therapy; continue PRN Lemsip as above; daytime cough suppressants not recommended, small dose at night acceptable if sleep severely disturbed.  
- Follow-up: Contact clinician if red-flag symptoms develop or if no improvement over next 7 days. Routine diabetes/BP check with GP as scheduled.  
- Patient questions addressed; patient in agreement with plan.

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits): Not recorded.  
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral: Not recorded.  
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support): Not recorded.  
- CTG registration: Not recorded.  
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test): Not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):

1. Acute viral upper respiratory tract infection / viral bronchitis – High likelihood (classic constellation of cough, rhinorrhoea, myalgias, feverishness over 5 days; no focal chest findings).  
2. COVID-19 infection – Moderate likelihood (similar symptom profile; diabetes is risk factor; no anosmia/dyspnoea reported).  
3. Post-viral acute bacterial sinusitis – Moderate likelihood (green nasal discharge and > 5 days symptoms, though lacks facial pain/tenderness).
